blocks.text: Atmospheric pressure is measured using a barometer. A barometer responds to pressure differences instead of measuring temperature or wind speed.
A thermometer measures temperature rather than atmospheric pressure. An anemometer measures wind speed, not atmospheric pressure.

claims.why: It changes with air pressure and does not directly measure temperature or wind speed.
claims.anchor: Atmospheric pressure is measured using a barometer.

claims.decision: A thermometer does not measure atmospheric pressure.
claims.why: Its measured quantity is temperature, which is different from pressure.
claims.anchor: A thermometer measures temperature rather than atmospheric pressure.

claims.decision: An anemometer does not measure atmospheric pressure.
claims.why: It measures wind speed, a different physical quantity from atmospheric pressure.
claims.anchor: An anemometer measures wind speed, not atmospheric pressure.
